title: Migrations: Bringing Models to Life
description: Turn your model definitions into actual database tables using Django's migration system.

slides.title: What Are Migrations? 🚚
slides.content:
A **migration** is a file that records changes to your models. Think of it as a version‑controlled history of your database schema.

When you add a new model or change an existing one, Django creates a migration that contains the SQL to update the database. You then **apply** the migration to your database.

> **Why migrations?** They keep your database schema in sync across different environments (local, staging, production).

slides.title: What Happens? 🧐
slides.content:
Django inspects your `models.py` and compares it to the last migration. It generates a new migration file inside `app/migrations/` (e.g., `0001_initial.py`).

You'll see output like:

```
Migrations for 'blog':
  blog/migrations/0001_initial.py
    - Create model Post
```

slides.title: Applying Migrations
slides.content: To actually create the tables in your database, run:

quizData.question: What is the correct order of commands when you add a new field to an existing model?
quizData.explanation: First create the migration file with `makemigrations`, then apply it with `migrate`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always commit migration files to version control

Migration files are part of your codebase. They ensure that anyone else (or your production server) can recreate the same database structure.
